web_evidence.title: Big Little Lies | Penguin Random House Retail
web_evidence.note: The publisher-hosted excerpt sustains third-person narration through Mrs. Ponder and Madeline across the opening chapters. Its labeled first-person parent statements are visibly interview/testimony snippets rather than the surrounding narrator.

web_evidence.title: “An Exquisite Suffering”: Representations of Maternal Ambivalence in 21st Century Texts About Motherhood
web_evidence.note: Rachel Williamson's University of Canterbury doctoral thesis explicitly describes the novel as using a shifting omniscient third-person narrative and separately identifies the Greek-chorus interviews as a framing device drawn from the novel.

web_evidence.title: Liane Moriarty Writing Styles in Big Little Lies
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly states that the novel is told in third-person omniscient, with chapters primarily shifting among Madeline, Jane, and Celeste, and distinguishes the parent interviews appended to chapters.

web_evidence.title: Interview with Liane Moriarty
web_evidence.note: Moriarty calls the short statements a 'suburban Greek chorus' and distinguishes them from scenes centered on Celeste and Madeline, confirming that their first-person speech is a local structural device rather than an alternate controlling narrator.

person_note: The controlling story is narrated in shifting third person, chiefly through Madeline, Jane, and Celeste. Several interior quote passages independently show sustained external narration and free-indirect access, agreeing with the authorized opening and the scholarly whole-book description. First-person material in the quote set is dialogue, quoted thought, or interview testimony; the author and structural sources identify the recurring interviews as short Greek-chorus framing snippets, not sustained first-person base sections, so they do not make the novel ALTERNATING. The publisher excerpt is limited to the opening, but the whole-book scholarly and study-guide evidence resolves that scope limitation; no material person conflict remains.
